note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, and Jesus and the people of the chapter are not portrayed: a father seen from behind or only as hands stands for the Father, and the healing is shown through ordinary people of today. Nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: A man helpless for thirty-eight years, with no one to carry him and always beaten to the water by others, is told "Rise, take up your mat, and walk," and at once he walks.
ideas: All round a still courtyard pool lie and sit many sick and disabled people of today, every one of them watching the water
A crowded hospital waiting room at night, every seat taken by the sick and lame, all watching the same closed door
A long line of sick people waits before dawn outside a free clinic that has not opened
A thin man on an old mat by the pool steps reaches for the water while others hurry past him into it
A man in a wheelchair at a bus stop as the crowd pushes onto the bus ahead of him and the doors close
An old man on a mat at the foot of a long staircase while people hurry up past him without a glance
A worn sleeping mat on bare ground, flattened by years of lying in one place
A thin man stands up on steady legs from his mat beside the pool, rolling it up, onlookers amazed
A man strides out through a gateway into a sunlit street with his rolled-up mat on his shoulder
Crutches left leaning against a wall as a man walks away down a sunny street

sections.meaning: The rule-keepers care more that a rule was broken than that a broken man was healed, and Jesus answers that his Father is always working, so he works too.
ideas: A stern official steps into the path of a beaming man carrying his rolled mat and points at the mat, frowning
A man dances for joy with his rolled mat over his head while a row of stern men in suits frown and point at the mat
A guard at a gate stops a man and taps the mat under his arm, unmoved by the joy on his face
A group of men in dark suits huddle in a plaza, whispering and glaring across at someone
A healed man walks out of a dark doorway into sunlight, turning his back on a dark alley
A father and his young son, seen from behind, build a stone wall side by side, both lifting stones
A father and his young son, seen from behind, paint the same wall with rollers, the work half done
A night nurse tends a patient while the whole city sleeps
Rain falls and crops grow in the fields on a quiet day when every shop is shut
A farmer is already out in his fields before dawn on the day everyone else rests

sections.meaning: The Son does nothing on his own but only what he sees the Father doing, because the Father loves him and shows him everything, and the Father has handed all judgment to the Son so that the Son is honored as the Father is.
ideas: A small boy's clay hands at a little potter's wheel copy exactly his father's hands at the big wheel beside him
A small boy at a little easel beside his father's big easel paints the very same stroke he watches his father paint
An apprentice watches over his father's shoulder as he planes a board, then makes the same stroke
A father guides his son's hands on a violin bow
A father bends close to show his son a delicate repair under a lamp, the son leaning in
An old father's hand places a heavy ring of keys into his grown son's open palm
An old father pulls out his own chair at the head of the family table for his grown son, and the family rises
An old farmer hands his son the keys of the farm truck in front of the barn
Workers of a family business greet the son with the same respect they show the father
A father lifts his son onto his shoulders so the son sees everything the father sees

sections.meaning: Whoever hears his word and trusts the one who sent him has already crossed over from death into life, and an hour is coming when even the dead will hear his voice and come out.
ideas: A man steps off a footbridge from a dead, frozen winter bank onto a bank in full green spring
A person walks out of a long dark tunnel into a sunlit green valley
A man steps over a fence from a dead brown field into a lush green one
A sleeper in a dark room lifts his head at a voice calling through a door full of morning light
A quiet graveyard at sunrise in spring with wildflowers burst up out of the ground over every grave
A field of bare winter earth with thousands of green shoots pushing up out of the soil at once
Children in a park at dusk hear their father call and come running out of every hiding place
A seed split open in dark soil with its first shoot reaching up into the light
Bare winter trees on one side of a path, blossoming trees on the other
Every door along a dark street opening at once at dawn

sections.meaning: Jesus does not vouch for himself: others testify for him, John the burning and shining lamp they enjoyed for a while, the works he does, the Father, and the scriptures they search, and still they will not come to him for life.
ideas: A witness stands in a courtroom with her right hand raised and points to the quiet man she is speaking for
At a meeting an older woman stands and speaks up for the silent man beside her, her hand on his shoulder
A single oil lantern hung on a post in a dark field, people dancing in its circle of light for a while
An old oil lamp burning on an outdoor table at night, a family laughing in its glow
A craftsman stands quietly aside while visitors admire the beautiful table he made
An empty wheelchair at the foot of a staircase while the man who sat in it climbs the stairs
A garden in full bloom speaks for the gardener whose hat and gloves lie on the bench
A man bends over a huge old book with a magnifying glass, his back to a door open onto a sunlit path
A man studies an old signpost over and over but never takes a step up the road it points to
A man reads an invitation again and again by his window while the lit house across the field waits with its door open

sections.meaning: They cannot believe because they live for praise from one another and do not seek the praise that comes from the only God.
ideas: A ring of people in formal clothes each pin a gold medal on the person beside them
A ring of people stand in a circle clapping for one another
A row of people turn their backs on a blazing sunrise to photograph themselves
A woman's face is lit by the likes on her phone while a glorious sky goes unseen behind her
A man on a stage bows to applause, basking in it
Two men hand each other trophies on a stage while a crowd applauds
A man admires the medals on his chest in a mirror
Guests at a dinner raise glasses to toast each other over and over
Dusty trophies on a shelf in an empty room
A crowd of cameras flashing at one smiling man

sections.meaning: The very writings they hope in accuse them, because Moses wrote about Jesus; not believing those writings, they will not believe his words.
ideas: A man clutches a treasured old book to his chest while its shadow on the wall points a finger back at him
A man walks away holding up a treasured old compass whose needle points back the way he left
An old letter held up in a courtroom against the man who treasured it
A man swears on an old book that he is right while its open page tells against him
A man walks away from an old signpost he has just read, the opposite way from its arrow
A man treasures his grandfather's old letter but turns away the visitor it describes
An old map in a man's hands shows a road to a town behind him, and he walks on the other way
A worn old book lies open on a table between two people facing each other
A man locks an old book in a glass case and never opens it
A man reads an old book by lamplight, then closes it and turns his back on the open door

candidates.prompt: A modern outdoor public pool in a quiet courtyard, ringed by a covered concrete walkway with plain square pillars. All along the pool's edge, on thin mats, benches and in wheelchairs, lie and sit many sick and disabled people of today: an old blind man in dark glasses holding a white cane, a woman with crutches beside her, a thin man lying on a thin mat. Every one of them is watching the still surface of the water, waiting. Soft overcast morning light. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A crowded hospital waiting room late at night under flat pale light: every seat is taken by sick and disabled people of today, some with crutches, some in wheelchairs, an old man lying across three chairs, a blind woman holding a white cane. All of them are turned toward the same closed door at the far end of the room, waiting for it to open. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a busy city street on a grey rainy afternoon, a thin middle-aged man in a wheelchair waits at the edge of a bus stop while a crowd of people push past him and climb onto the bus ahead of him. The bus doors are closing and there is no room left. No one looks at him; he watches the closing doors, alone. The man and the closing bus doors are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

At the edge of a modern outdoor pool, a thin, worn man lies on a thin old mat beside the steps that lead down into the water, propped on one elbow and reaching one hand toward the water. All around him other people hurry past him and step down into the pool ahead of him, splashing in. No one helps him. Soft daylight. His face and the hurrying people are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a bright clear morning, a man in plain everyday clothes walks out through an open gateway into a sunlit street, carrying a rolled-up sleeping mat on his shoulder. He walks with strong, steady steps, smiling with amazed happiness. Behind him, in the shade of a courtyard, people sitting beside a pool turn to watch him go. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

Beside a modern outdoor pool on a bright morning, a man in plain everyday clothes has just stood up from the sleeping mat on the ground where he lay for years. He stands tall and steady, rolling the mat up under his arm, his face full of wonder. People sitting round the pool look up at him in amazement. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a sunny city plaza, a happy man in plain clothes walks along carrying a rolled-up sleeping mat on his shoulder. A serious official in a dark suit stands in front of him, frowning and pointing at the mat with a disapproving look, while two more officials in dark suits stand behind him with folded arms. The faces and the mat are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a city street, a thin man in plain worn clothes dances for joy, holding his rolled-up old sleeping mat high over his head. On the steps of an office building beside him, a row of stern men in dark suits frown down at him, pointing at the mat and shaking their heads. Bright afternoon light, clear sky. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a green hillside farm on a bright, breezy morning with white clouds, a father and his young son, both seen from behind, work side by side building a dry stone wall across the field, each of them lifting a stone onto the wall at the same moment. The long wall already stretches away behind them, the work well under way. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a clear bright day, a father and his young son, both seen from behind, stand side by side painting the same white wall of a house with paint rollers, both reaching up and working hard. The wall is half done, fresh and bright where they have painted. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

Close view in a sunny pottery workshop: a father's strong clay-covered hands shape a bowl on a big potter's wheel, and right beside it a small boy's clay-covered hands shape his own little bowl on a small wheel, held in exactly the same way. The boy's face, seen in profile, is turned to watch his father's hands closely. The father is seen only as hands and arms. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a bright attic art studio, a small boy stands at a little easel beside his father's big easel, both seen from behind. The boy watches his father's brush and paints the very same stroke on his own small canvas; the two paintings, one large and one small, are the same picture of hills and sky. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

Close view in warm window light: an old father's weathered hand places a heavy ring of old iron keys into the open palm of his grown son's hand. Only the two hands and the keys are seen, filling the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a family dining room at a long table crowded with family, an old grey-haired father, seen from behind, pulls out his own big chair at the head of the table for his grown son, who steps forward to take it, seen from the side. Everyone round the table is rising to their feet in respect. Soft daylight. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A man in plain clothes, seen from behind, steps off the end of a narrow wooden footbridge across a stream. The bank he has left behind is grey and dead: bare frozen trees and dead grass under old snow. The bank he steps onto bursts with green spring grass, wildflowers and leafy trees in bright light. The bridge and both banks are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A person in plain clothes, seen from behind, walks out of the mouth of a long dark tunnel into a bright green valley full of daylight and wildflowers, the darkness of the tunnel all around the edges of the frame behind them. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A wide field of bare dark earth just after a spring rain in the early morning: all across it, thousands of fresh green shoots are pushing up out of the soil at once, standing up toward the light. Low mist and soft clear light. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A quiet old country graveyard of plain weathered headstones on a green hillside at sunrise in spring: light floods across the grass, and fresh wildflowers have burst up out of the ground over every grave, all open toward the light. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a plain modern courtroom, a woman stands at the witness stand with her right hand raised, speaking firmly, and with her other hand points across the room toward a quiet man seated alone, seen from behind, who says nothing. The people on the benches turn to look at him. Even daylight from tall windows. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

At a community meeting in a plain hall with rows of chairs, an older woman has stood up from her seat and speaks up for the quiet man sitting beside her, one hand on his shoulder; he sits silent with his hands folded, seen from the side. The people in the rows have turned round to listen to her. Soft daylight. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

At night in a dark open field, a single bright oil lantern hangs from a tall wooden post, burning and shining, and a crowd of people of today are gathered in its warm circle of light, laughing and dancing. All around them the field is dark. The lantern and the dancers are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a summer night, an old oil lamp burns brightly in the middle of an outdoor wooden table, and a family sits round it laughing together in its warm glow, faces lit; all around them the garden is dark. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a sunlit woodworking shop, a craftsman in a work apron stands quietly off to one side, seen from behind, while visitors gather round a beautiful finished wooden table he has made, running their hands over it in admiration. The table and the admiring visitors are the centre of the picture. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a bright hospital hallway, an empty wheelchair stands at the foot of a staircase, and the man who sat in it is climbing the stairs on his own two feet, holding the rail, while a nurse at the bottom of the stairs holds her hands over her mouth in wonder. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a dim study, a man bends low over a huge old open book on a desk, peering at it through a magnifying glass, searching it line by line. Behind his back a door stands wide open onto a bright sunlit garden path, and he never turns to look at it. The man, the book and the bright open door are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

At a crossroads in open green country, a man stands close up to an old wooden signpost, studying its blank wooden arrow intently as if reading it over and over. The arrow points up a sunlit road to a welcoming house on a hill with its door open, but the man has not taken a single step. Bright clear afternoon. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a grand hall, a ring of people in formal suits and gowns stand in a circle facing inward, each one pinning a shiny gold medal onto the chest of the person beside them, all smiling at one another. Every chest already gleams with medals. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

On a mountain overlook at dawn, a row of people stand with their backs to a magnificent sunrise blazing over the peaks behind them, every one of them holding up a phone to photograph themselves, their faces lit by their own screens. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a plain room lit by a single lamp, a man clutches a treasured old leather book tight to his chest. On the wall behind him, the shadow of the book has become a large pointing hand, its finger aimed straight back at him. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A man in a plain coat walks along a path across a wide open moor on a cloudy day, holding up an old brass compass he clearly treasures. The compass needle points straight back behind him, toward a bright town on a hill in the distance that he is walking away from. The important part is in the upper two thirds of the picture.

Beside a plain outdoor pool in a quiet concrete courtyard, where many sick and disabled people sit and lie on old mats and in wheelchairs, a gaunt middle-aged man in old worn clothes has just got up from the ground where he lay for years. He walks away on his own two feet, carrying his old rolled-up bedroll blanket under one arm, his face full of astonished joy, while the sick people round the pool stare after him with their mouths open, one of them pointing. Soft morning light. The man and the staring people are in the upper two thirds of the picture.
